newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Strike by South African sugar workers drags on.
newsitem.headline: Strike by South African sugar workers drags on.

text.p: A strike by thousands of South African sugar workers entered its 13th day on Monday as the industry said it was planning to recover most of the lost production.
Fourteen mills and refineries owned by Illovo Sugar Ltd and Tongaat-Hulett Ltd have been closed since July 2 as a result of a wage strike by over 4,000 workers.
The strike was costing the industry about 83,500 tonnes of cane per day in lost production but the industry has declined to put a value to the losses.

Bheki Sibiya, the spokesman for both companies, said there were still five months left in the crushing season, which began in April, and the industry was considering various options to recover lost production.
"There are a lot of things that can be done to recover some, or most, of the lost production.
"Until these plans are discussed by all the role players any figures released will remain pure speculation," Sibiyba told Reuters.
Sibiya said a meeting would be held with union representatives on either Tuesday or Wednesday.
A union spokesman said the major sticking point was the reluctance of the employers to backdate an 11.5 percent wage increase to April 1. Employers want to backdate the increase to June 1.
"We are so very close to an agreement," said Eric Botha.
The unions and employers said on Friday they hoped the strike would be resolved this week and that production could be resumed late in the week.
